latest_user_contract.lifetime: Closing a local terminal, losing SSH, browser disconnect or explicit detach never destroys the workspace. It persists in a user-owned supervisor and private bundled tmux server. Only explicit terminal stop, exit/Ctrl+D closing the final shell, or explicitly configured idle/session timeout ends it. Earlier end-on-owner-disconnect proposal is superseded.
latest_user_contract.expiry: Invitation expiry prevents NEW joins only. Already attached participants continue without timer-driven resets. Browser reconnection credentials must preserve the same participant role independently of invitation expiry. Standard SSH connections remain alive until they disconnect/end/revoke; do not claim impossible transparent TCP reconnect for stock SSH clients.
latest_user_contract.attach: Support terminal attach NAME/ID from the host, including sessions started with --detach and sessions whose original SSH terminal closed. --detach only controls initial attachment, not persistence.
latest_user_contract.names: Generate friendly random lowercase letters-only names such as amberotter or quietfalcon when --name is omitted. Do not insert hyphens or other separators: double-click should select the entire generated name. Check collisions, keep internal random session IDs separate, and accept names in attach/list/stop/management commands.
latest_user_contract.participant_panel: Right-side participant list in browser and native host workspace, with readable participant identities/roles and owner eviction controls. Eviction revokes that participant's reconnect credential without terminating other users or shells. Account for tmux/SSH resizes and small screens.
latest_user_contract.multiplexer: Full bundled tmux engine/features on Linux/macOS; panes, windows, layouts, resizing, names, scrollback, search, copy mode and configuration access. No separately installed tmux/libevent/ncurses/terminfo needed. Windows SSH/browser participants supported; native Windows hosting needs a separate backend and must be clearly documented if not shipped.
latest_user_contract.keys: Default Ctrl+A prefix, configurable; double prefix sends the literal key. Avoid requiring Ctrl+B. Visible help/menu and browser controls as alternatives; no claim that any key bypasses all terminal/OS shortcuts.
latest_user_contract.scroll_copy: Match inspected ~/.tmux.conf: mouse scrolling/select/resize, 100000 history lines and F7 copy/scroll mode toggle. Preserve drag-to-copy with supported client clipboard behavior; browser copy permissions and SSH OSC52/nested tmux constraints must be tested/documented. Read-only viewers must be able to browse history without sending shell input.
latest_user_contract.transport: Use the existing optimized PortHub peer transport for PortHub-aware terminal participants: prefer an authenticated direct route when reachable and fall back to the gateway relay, preserving session identity, permissions and shared state. Browser peers require an explicitly implemented browser-compatible direct transport with relay fallback; do not claim direct browser routing until tested. Ordinary unmodified SSH guests use the public SSH gateway and cannot automatically participate in the PortHub peer protocol. Prioritize interactive input/control over bulk/history transfer, bound queues, support cancellation and avoid reconnecting the workspace when a transport changes.
latest_user_contract.local: Provide local persistent tmux-style workspaces without sharing, registration or network access: terminal new/list/attach/stop, detached tasks, full panes/windows/history. Local and shared workspaces use the same engine; sharing is optional.
latest_user_contract.nested_attach: Owner attach must work inside another tmux session without the nesting warning. Recognize the same private workspace and avoid recursive attachment; remote PTY attachments always connect as independent clients to the same shared session.
latest_user_contract.named_open: porthub terminal NAME is the primary ergonomic local entry point: attach to a running workspace of that name, or create one if absent/ended. --detach opens/creates without local attachment. Preserve ended records in an archive and assign a fresh internal identity on recreation. Explicit new/attach remain optional advanced commands.

architecture.terminal_crate: New porthub-terminal protocol/hub crate with optional russh SSH gateway feature. Current core tests and real OpenSSH interactive/read-only test pass. Agent need not compile SSH server crypto.
architecture.gateway: API hosts SSH over private Unix socket with persistent Ed25519 key. Edge fixed-destination TCP ingress planned for 8347; no forwarding to a machine sshd. Public browser joins authenticate by first WebSocket message, keeping invite tokens out of query strings/logs. Metadata/hashes/revocation persisted in Mongo; terminal contents not logged/stored.
architecture.agent: User CLI/supervisor owns shells and private multiplexer, not the privileged service. Existing OS-authenticated local broker will authenticate the host's WebSocket using machine credentials without disclosing them to the CLI.
architecture.helper: Static musl tmux 3.8 bundle built and exercised locally. Separate helper CI cache; embedded bytes and content-addressed private extraction with target/file checksum/link/permission checks; active workspaces retain their original helper. All-platform CI and release validation pending.

current_limits.platforms: Hosting currently implemented on Unix using bundled tmux. Linux native static helper validated. macOS/all-platform packaging not yet validated; native Windows hosting not implemented. Ordinary SSH and browser guests do not require the PortHub CLI.
current_limits.clipboard: Browser Copy selection and opt-in copy-on-selection use the local Clipboard API and require browser permission/secure context; browser menu Copy remains the fallback. No remote clipboard reads/writes are enabled. Native OSC52 support depends on the outer terminal/SSH client and its permissions.
current_limits.history: Tmux retains the configured history (100000 lines by default). Browser captures are read-only live slices, with explicit 128KiB response bounds and adjustable page size; navigation and search do not fetch the entire transcript. New output/resizing can shift page boundaries, so stable snapshot anchoring is still pending. Native read-only SSH supports independent F7 history, wheel, arrows, PageUp/PageDown and Home/End, with a targeted redraw when returning live. Captures are rate-limited live slices; stable anchors and richer Unicode grapheme clipping remain pending. Ordinary interactive clients retain tmux copy mode.
current_limits.disconnect: Workspace survives attachment/transport disconnect. Browser recovers with a separate tab-scoped bearer credential, independent of invitation expiry, within Options.reconnect_timeout (10–300 seconds after disconnect). Active sockets renew their lease, so connected guests are not interrupted by that deadline. Retrying uses bounded backoff. Tab closure clears sessionStorage; a fresh tab needs a valid invitation.
current_limits.eviction: CLI kick revokes that guest recovery credential and closes only that guest. Revocation persists across API restart. Holders of a still-valid public invitation can intentionally join as a new guest; invitation rotation/renewal controls remain required.
current_limits.transport: Browser and ordinary SSH guests currently relay through gateway. Optimized aware-client direct routing and a browser-compatible direct transport remain required.
current_limits.browser_management: Login is optional for terminal participation. Browser guest management requires an authenticated current workspace owner/admin for the registered machine. An unrelated account or global site-admin role alone does not grant machine administration. Permission is checked on every management request; UI capability checks are bounded and refreshed on visibility changes.
current_limits.permission_boundary: Browser management UI/API is account-authorized independently of invitation access. Interactive terminal guests execute as the host OS user in the shared shell, just as tmux/tmate participants do; they therefore retain that OS user’s command and file permissions. Read-only guests cannot send shell input. UI authorization is not a sandbox for interactive shell commands.

invitation_rotation_checkpoint.status: CLI --rotate/--renew and --link-expires, private durable pending state, retry after process loss and authenticated gateway persistence are implemented. Source only; browser rotation controls and full CLI-to-live-gateway release validation remain pending.
invitation_rotation_checkpoint.semantics: Fresh capability pair and bounded revision replace new-join mappings atomically. The new expiry is independent of immutable workspace options. Current guests and verified recovery retain their role. Matching retries are idempotent and cannot reopen a subsequently revoked revision. Old hosts, conflicting revisions and cross-session token collisions are rejected. Capability identity is rechecked atomically during final admission.
invitation_rotation_checkpoint.tests: Real bundled CLI/supervisor fixture passes: kills worker before acknowledgement, reconstructs it, verifies identical pending replay and immutable host identity, prints confirmed new URLs, retains shell variables, blocks revoked links, renews after revocation and explicitly stops. Filesystem failure/private replay unit passes. Normal agent library suite passes 69 tests (two environment-specific tests skipped). Nineteen terminal core tests, five actual bundled tmux tests and ordinary OpenSSH test pass. Six Chromium guide checks pass across dark/light and 1440/402/320px. Gateway restart and authenticated WebSocket rotation tests passed in preceding checkpoint; the CLI fixture uses an isolated broker protocol simulator, not a live gateway.
invitation_rotation_checkpoint.gateway_semantics: A new rotation must be exactly the next durable revision. Gateway commits only hashes/expiry/revision before replacing live routes, then acknowledges the revision. Matching retries return durable revoked state without reopening links. Original host identity and workspace options remain immutable. Expired replacement links still permit the authenticated workspace host to reconnect.
invitation_rotation_checkpoint.host_semantics: The supervisor saves and syncs a pending capability pair before sending. Plain invite withholds links while pending. CLI waits for a matching gateway acknowledgement, and the supervisor replays the same revision and pair after Ready on reconnect/restart. A failed save rolls back the in-memory pending update. Matching acknowledgement saves confirmed state before exposing the revision. Expired pending lifetimes may be confirmed as already expired to resolve ambiguity; a subsequent rotation issues a fresh lifetime.

native_participant_popup.status: Implemented and locally tested; cross-platform/release validation pending.
native_participant_popup.interaction: Local owner CLI attachments hold a private file lock for the child tmux client. Prefix then capital P opens a targeted right-side popup with existing participant selection and removal. q closes the focused popup and returns to the shell; it does not add a shell pane. Width is bounded by actual client width. Shortcut failures are quiet and do not trigger shared copy mode.
native_participant_popup.authority: The popup checks a private live owner-attachment lease and resolves the matching tmux PID to its client TTY. Unregistered client IDs and stale unlocked leases fail. This is OS-user-scoped native control, not a sandbox against interactive guests who already have the host shell OS permissions. Browser management remains separately account-authorized.
native_participant_popup.tests: Actual PTYs pass at 100 and 36 columns: selection, confirmation cancellation, selected removal, resize, q return and owner detach; validates no additional pane and retained workspace. Unregistered process and stale unlocked lease rejected. Existing full-screen stalled-control test also passes. Local CLI workspace/share regressions pass, including persisted shell state, invitation rotation process-loss recovery and explicit stop.
native_participant_popup.limits: A focused popup, not a continuously visible nonmodal split. Cross-platform CI now runs native terminal and popup checks in verify-only mode as well as final packaged tests.
native_participant_popup.macos_test_fixture: Darwin invalidates slave termios reads after the controlling session ends. The PTY harness now retains a small controlling session leader, captures the application-restored mode while the session still exists, then returns the application exit status. It preserves the full restoration assertion; it does not skip Darwin verification. Linux PTY checks pass after this fixture change; Darwin CI rerun required. The next Darwin check exposed a before/after mismatch; the fixture now captures both baselines inside the retained controlling session and reports detailed flags if they differ. This preserves the restoration assertion; Darwin rerun remains required.

input_pressure_validation.finding: Mixed real browser/API/SSH/tmux pressure reproduced a host command truncated after roughly sixteen single-character messages. The native PTY input channel was bounded by sixteen messages and could close the attachment under ordinary short typing bursts. The failed Chromium run retained its native shell capture, proving an actual partial command rather than only a DOM observation timeout.
input_pressure_validation.fix: PTY input now uses a 64KiB byte buffer with 16KiB write batches and one coalesced wake notification. Overflow remains bounded and disconnects only the affected viewer. Worker writes occur outside the buffer mutex; detach clears queued input.
input_pressure_validation.evidence: Deterministic unit verifies 4000 individual keystrokes retain order, 64KiB overflow is rejected without partial enqueue, batch size is bounded and clearing works. Twenty core tests, six real bundled tmux tests and ordinary OpenSSH pass. Combined Chromium and WebKit flows pass six recovery cycles/eight attachments with concurrent shell output/history and role/identity preservation. Final Chromium and WebKit flows also assert the host retained one WebSocket for the entire run; both pass.
input_pressure_validation.limits: This establishes the specific PTY queue fix and bounded mixed-pressure scenario; it does not retroactively prove the cause of an earlier intermittent WebKit timeout or replace sustained production monitoring.

history_scheduling.problem: A continuously ready PTY output queue could indefinitely starve the separately bounded history queue because selection always preferred live output.
history_scheduling.fix: Retain live-output preference but service one waiting history chunk after at most eight live messages. No output or control frames are dropped.
history_scheduling.evidence: Deterministic queue regression fails before the fix and passes after it. Twenty-one core tests, six real bundled multiplexer tests, ordinary OpenSSH and the combined Chromium and WebKit browser/API/edge/bundled-shell history/recovery/admin flow pass.
history_scheduling.remaining: Stable history snapshot anchors remain pending; scheduling fairness does not prevent live output, eviction or resizing from shifting history rows.

terminal_helper_cache_isolation.diagnosis: Run 41233783102 produced an x86 helper bundle and then lost it before Rust embedding; upstream Swatinem/rust-cache v2 restore code cleans target directories on a partial cache match. Keeping helper source/output beneath Cargo target allowed that cleanup to remove bundles and leave empty source directories. ARMhf also saw a source-download network failure.
terminal_helper_cache_isolation.fix: CI helper sources/output and their separate restore/save cache now live at .cache/terminal-helper, outside Cargo target, selected by absolute PORTHUB_TERMINAL_HELPER_CACHE_ROOT. Rust builds fail early if the helper bundle is absent after cache restore. Dedicated helper build log uploads include that hidden directory explicitly. Local/Docker target cache defaults stay unchanged.
terminal_helper_cache_isolation.validation: Actionlint and the two real compiler/ELF helper-gate tests pass. Corrected 32-bit packaged jobs still need execution; no release is validated or deployed by these checks.

ssh_on_existing_tls_port.implementation: Optional PORTHUB_TERMINAL_SSH_MULTIPLEX=true enables SSH/HTTPS protocol selection on existing PortHub TLS listeners. The edge peeks one byte without consuming TLS data, forwards SSH only to the fixed API Unix socket, limits forwarded SSH connections to 64 across TLS listeners and bounds silent identification to three seconds. Default remains disabled. API capability authentication, roles, recovery and revocation are unchanged. Explicit --api-socket also supplies the derived SSH socket default.
ssh_on_existing_tls_port.validation: All thirty-one edge tests pass, including six new selection/forwarding/quota/shutdown/deadline cases. Real Chromium and WebKit browser/API/bundled-shell/ordinary OpenSSH flows pass on the shared TLS port with 78 and 104 fresh concurrent HTTPS connections. A one-second TLS handshake budget does not truncate the longer-lived SSH guests. Both original dedicated-listener and multiplexed WebKit flows pass. Compose default-off and enabled/shared-port settings pass.
ssh_on_existing_tls_port.deployment: PortHub owns a reachable public TLS listener on 443 at URM2; dedicated 8347 probes did not reach the host. The new mode provides a deployment option on existing 443. Newly built images are required; previously staged source-82e300c images do not contain this mode. Production remains unchanged. Direct SSH hostname must bypass HTTP-only CDNs; HTTPS-payload-only middleboxes may still block raw SSH.
